connect.rule: 普通形 ＋ {にもかかわらず}
〜（である）／〜だった ＋ {にもかかわらず}

examples.ja: 彼はまだ初心者である{にもかかわらず}、市のテニス大会で三位に入った。
examples.en: Even though he is still a beginner, he came third in the city tennis tournament.

examples.ja: 値段が高い{にもかかわらず}、この店のパンは昼前に売り切れる。
examples.en: Even though it is expensive, this shop's bread sells out before noon.

watch.note: にもかかわらず is formal, and what follows it is a fact that goes against what you expect. It cannot lead to a request, an invitation or an order. For those, use ても.
watch.bad: 雨にもかかわらず、出かけましょう。
watch.good: 雨でも、出かけましょう。

connect.rule: 知ります → 知り ＋ {つつ（も）}
飲みます → 飲み ＋ {つつ}

examples.ja: 駐車禁止だと知り{つつも}、少しの間だけならと道の端に車を止めてしまった。
examples.en: I knew parking was not allowed, but I left the car at the side of the road, thinking a few minutes would do no harm.

examples.ja: 朝はコーヒーを飲み{つつ}、ニュースをチェックするのが習慣だ。
examples.en: In the morning I always check the news while drinking my coffee.

watch.note: つつ（も） joins verbs only, in the ます stem, and one person does both things. After an adjective or a noun, use ながら（も）, which you met at N3.
watch.bad: 忙しいつつも、毎日運動している。
watch.good: 忙しいながらも、毎日運動している。

compare.intro: All three join two facts that clash. にもかかわらず is formal and states facts, つつも keeps one person doing both, and のに adds the speaker's own feeling and can even end a sentence.

forms.ja: 卒業して二十年たっていた{にもかかわらず}、先生は私の名前を覚えていてくださった。
forms.en: Twenty years had passed since I graduated, yet my teacher still remembered my name.

forms.ja: 初めての発表で緊張し{つつも}、最後までしっかり話すことができた。
forms.en: I was nervous at my first presentation, but I spoke clearly all the way to the end.

forms.tag: 不満・残念 · even though (and I'm upset)
forms.ja: せっかく早く来た{のに}、店は休みだった。
forms.en: I made the effort to come early, and the shop was closed.

check.label: 花火大会の中止
check.q: 「明日の花火大会、雨で中止になったそうですよ。」「えっ、[浴衣|ゆかた]まで買った（　　）。」
why: The reply stops right after the blank, with no clashing fact to follow. にもかかわらず is not used to end a spoken complaint the way のに is.
つつも follows the ます stem (買い), not the た form, and the reply has no second part for it to lead to.
のに can end a sentence to show regret or a complaint: "and I even bought a yukata!"

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: ^住所を正しく書いて送った^（　　）、^荷物が相手に届かなかった^。
why: ことから gives a reason or the grounds for a judgement. A correct address is no reason for a parcel not to arrive.
The address was right, yet the parcel did not arrive: a fact that goes against what you expect.
あげく follows a long, tiring process, as in 何時間も話し合ったあげく. Sending a parcel is not one.
せいで blames a cause for a bad result, but the correct address did not stop the parcel arriving.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: 彼は毎回（　　）、^同じミスを繰り返している^。
why: からには needs a resolve or a duty after it, such as 二度としない. Repeating the mistake is the opposite.
おかげで gives the cause of a good result, and a repeated mistake is not one.
ばかりに gives the cause of a bad result. Reflecting does not cause the mistake.
He is sorry each time, yet he does it again: ます stem + つつも, one person doing both.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: ^早朝^（　　）、隣の家から^工事の大きな音が聞こえてきた^。
why: A noun goes straight before にもかかわらず. Early morning, yet loud building work: not what you expect.
につき gives a formal reason, as on a notice (祝日につき休業). Early morning is no reason for the noise.
を機に means "taking the chance of" a change, as in 入学を機に. Early morning is not such a chance.
に際して marks a formal occasion, as in 入場に際して. Early morning is not an occasion.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: ^地図を^（　　）、^知らない町を歩いて回った^。
why: 以上 needs a duty or a judgement after it. Walking around is a plain past event.
次第 means "as soon as" and leads to an action still to come, not a past event like 回った.
Two actions at once by one person, in written style: ます stem + つつ, like ながら.
あまり needs a feeling or an effort taken too far, and an unusual result. Walking around is not one.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.hint: What does 熱が need right after it? 大事な describes a noun.
drill.full: 彼女は熱があった{にもかかわらず}大事な会議に出席したそうだ。
drill.explain: 熱が takes あった, and にもかかわらず follows the plain form. 大事な describes 会議, and 会議に goes with 出席した.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.hint: Which tile is a ます stem? What was chosen in the end?
drill.full: どちらにするか迷い{つつも}青いかばんに決めた。
drill.explain: 迷い is the ます stem of 迷う, so つつも follows it. 青い describes かばん, and かばんに goes with 決めた.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: その会社は経営が苦しい（　　）、今年も社員の給料を上げた。
exam.explain: Business is hard, yet the company raised pay again: a fact that goes against what you expect, so にもかかわらず. ばかりに leads to a regretted result, だけあって to a result that lives up to the cause, and 以上 to a judgement or a duty, not a report of what happened like 上げた.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: 母は口では（　　）、私の留学の準備を手伝ってくれた。
exam.explain: My mother opposed it in words, yet she helped: one person doing two things that clash, so つつも. 以上 leads to a judgement or a duty, not a past event like 手伝ってくれた, 次第 to an action still to come, and せいで to a bad result.

exam.label: Build the sentence
exam.full: あれだけ宣伝したにもかかわらず{新商品の}売り上げは伸びなかった。
exam.explain: 宣伝した, にもかかわらず, 新商品の, 売り上げは. にもかかわらず follows the plain form, and 新商品の must sit right before 売り上げは.

scene.intro: Tap every word on the results sheet you would need to understand.

check.label: How the exam asks it
check.q: 検査の結果、特に_異常_は見つからなかった。
check.explain: 異常 is いじょう: 異 is イ, and 常 is ジョウ as in 正常 and 日常. いしょう is a different word (衣装, costume), and いじょ and いぞう are not readings of 異常.

skill.ask: What finally made the writer go for his follow-up test?
skill.passage: 去年の健康診断で、血圧が基準値を超えているので再検査を受けるようにと言われた。しかし、体調は特に悪くなかった。行かなければと思いつつも、仕事の忙しさを理由に後回しにしていた。妻に何度も勧められたにもかかわらず、結局半年も病院に行かなかった。^ところが^今年の春、^同い年の友人が突然倒れて入院した^。彼も以前から血圧が高いと言われていたが、何もしていなかったという。^その話を聞いて^、私はようやく病院に電話をかけた。^自分だけは大丈夫だと、勝手に思い込んでいた^のだ。
skill.strategy: Find where the story turns (ところが), then read what the writer did right after it and why.

item.q: 筆者が再検査を受けることにしたのは、なぜか。
options: 妻に何度も勧められて、断れなくなったから。
仕事が落ち着いて、時間ができたから。
友人のことを聞いて、自分も危ないと気づいたから。
体調が悪くなって、不安になったから。
short: 自分も危ないと気づいた
item.explain: The story turns at ところが: a friend his age, also told his blood pressure was high, collapsed. その話を聞いて, the writer finally called the hospital. He saw that he had only assumed he would be fine (勝手に思い込んでいた).
why: His wife urged him many times, but he still did not go (にもかかわらず). That is not what changed his mind.
Not in the text. Work is only the excuse he used for putting it off.
Not in the text. He felt fine (体調は特に悪くなかった), and nothing says that changed. His friend's story is what made him call.
